previous_statement: Let (u_pol,h_pol) be the inverse supplied by 1.7.4 for Pi_delta: calU x B_delta^{calH}(J) -> S_delta. Uniqueness of this inverse identifies u_grp with u_pol only after proving that X maps to (u_grp(X),h(X)) is a two-sided inverse of that very Pi_delta with the same source and target (for some h).
new_statement: Let (u_pol,h_pol):S_delta -> calU x B_delta^{calH}(J) be the inverse supplied by 1.7.4 for Pi_delta:calU x B_delta^{calH}(J) -> S_delta. A global two-sided inverse built from u_grp is sufficient but not necessary for identifying first components. More minimally, for any X in S_delta it suffices to know that u_grp(X) lies in calU and to exhibit h_X in B_delta^{calH}(J) with Pi_delta(u_grp(X),h_X)=X: the inverse identity for (u_pol,h_pol) and injectivity of Pi_delta then give u_grp(X)=u_pol(X). Thus, for the parent transport, pointwise preimage identities at every relevant X=U bold-dot V and X=U^dagger (together with membership of those X in S_delta) would suffice; the allowed group-laws external supplies neither these identities nor any other synchronization with this explicit Pi_delta.
